transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Endless Rain [H-01], Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple [L-02].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The causeway is a spine of black timber and drowned stone, and the four of you have walked it since first light with the rain never once letting up. Ahead, through the grey curtain, the stilt-legs of Hollowmoot rise out of the flood like a heron's roost, cook-smoke bent flat by the wind. Behind you the Sallowmere stretches away in sheets of standing water, reed-tops nodding, the old road already swallowed to a rumor beneath the mire. Somewhere off in the wet a bell that isn't a bell — thin, wrong, almost sung — carries and fades. You need to reach the gate before Hollowmoot bars its doors at dark, or spend the night in open water with whatever the rain is hiding.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: That sound—the temples make it, or something in them makes it. We need Hollowmoot's gate open before dark, or we're spending the night in the water with whatever that is.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde's jaw tightens as the thin, wrong bell-sound carries through the rain. She quickens her pace along the black timber causeway, eyes fixed on Hollowmoot's distant stilt-legs rising through the grey curtain. Her hand moves instinctively to the scroll case at her hip—Tamsin's dead scholar's voice echoing in her memory, warnings annotated in margins about temple sounds, Order wards, and the things that dwell in drowned places.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: That bell—it's coming from the drowned temple ahead. The rain carries its voice for a reason.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous halts on the causeway and closes his eyes, rain streaming down his face. He tilts his head to catch that thin, wrong sound, reading it like he reads the rainfall itself.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: That sound in the rain—that's no natural bell. Stay sharp, everyone. We move toward the gate, but we keep our eyes open.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire's hand settles on the hilt of her blade, her jaw tightening. The years of watch drills snap into place as she scans the grey sheets ahead, tracking the way the sound moves through the water. Her shoulders set into the familiar stance of someone expecting trouble and ready to meet it head-on.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - - - 0, invoking Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01] → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous goes still on the causeway, rain sheeting off his hood, and lets the wrong-bell sound wash over him the way he's learned to read the rain itself — its rhythm, its pauses, the way it bends. It isn't random. The tone stutters every few heartbeats, like something vast drawing breath before it sings again, and beneath it he catches the shape of the thing: not a bell at all, but a voice, and it is calling from the belltower, not the nave. He opens his eyes and grabs Ysolde's sleeve. "It pulses — there's a rhythm to it, like it's breathing. When it stops, that's when something's listening instead of singing. We can move in the gaps." The others feel it too now, an omen read clean out of the storm: the safest moment to move will be the quiet between two verses of that drowned hymn.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The Order stitches hymns into drowned temples—Tamsin's scrolls taught me their language. When it breathes out, we move. Now.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde squeezes Aldous's wrist once in firm acknowledgment, her other hand moving instinctively to Tamsin's scroll case at her hip as if drawing strength from her dead teacher's warnings. She turns sharply to Morwen and Mire with a savage nod, jaw set hard. As the thin, wrong bell-voice reaches its peak and holds for one shuddering breath, she watches it—waiting, waiting—and then as it fractures into silence, she steps forward into the rain-curtain, gesturing urgently for the others to follow in the gaps Aldous has found, moving through the pauses between verses of that drowned hymn like a crew threading needles in a storm.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Listen—when it sings, that's our moment. When the voice rises, we move. The instant it stops, we go absolutely still. Those gaps between verses are when it listens, when it hunts. Ready yourselves.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous keeps his grip on Ysolde's sleeve, his other hand raised to signal the others. He's counting the rhythm silently, his rain-soaked face turned toward the sound, waiting for the next verse to surge through the storm. When it does, he'll pull them forward along the causeway toward Hollowmoot's gate.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The gaps—that's when we move. Aldous, you count that rhythm for us; I'll hold point and get us to the gate before dark catches us.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire nods sharply at Aldous, drawing her blade with a soft ring of steel—not for threat, but for readiness. She moves to the front of the group, gesturing them into the tight formation she learned in the Temple Orphanage's watch drills. As the wrong-bell swells toward its listening silence, she signals forward, leading them into the gap between verses, her eyes fixed on Hollowmoot's distant stilt-legs rising through the grey curtain. She holds the line the way she was trained to, even disgraced.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous's count never breaks. Three times the wrong-bell rises and holds and cracks into silence, and three times Mire drives them forward through the gap like she's still running a Wardens' drill — Ysolde close behind with a hand pressed to Tamsin's scroll case to keep the rain from its pages, Morwen bringing up the rear with an eye on the black water either side of the causeway. On the last silence they hit the gate-stair at a run, timbers slick and canting underfoot, just as a soaked Warden on the parapet above shouts down for the bar to drop. He sees four shapes lunge out of the grey — weighs them for a breath, torch guttering — and waves them through instead of through the eye of a nocked crossbow. The gate-bar slams home behind them with a boom that briefly, blessedly, drowns out the belltower's voice. Hollowmoot closes around you: crowded stilt-walks, dripping eaves, the smell of woodsmoke and too many wet bodies in too little dry space — and somewhere behind you, out in the flood, the drowned hymn starts its next verse to an audience that got away.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The gate-bar booms shut and Hollowmoot swallows you whole: a warren of slick stilt-walkways strung between leaning houses, lantern-light bleeding gold through oiled-cloth windows, gutters roaring with runoff. Folk here move fast and don't meet your eyes — doors are already being barred early tonight, and somewhere a crier's bell (a real one, human-rung) is calling the last stragglers in before dusk. A Warden sergeant named Coss, soaked to the bone and clearly rattled by that drowned hymn carrying over the water, plants himself at the top of the gate-stair to look you over properly now that there's torchlight to see by — he wants to know who you are, why you were out past the ford this late, and whether any of you have so much as a scratch on you. Behind him, the town waits: dry beds are few, doors close at dark, and everyone with a fire seems to already know something about that sound from the temple that they aren't saying out loud.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Sergeant—that sound from the temple shook you as much as it shook us. We came from the ford and it followed us all the way. Has it been calling like that long, or is this something new?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward calmly, her hands open and loose at her sides, making direct eye contact with Coss. Her jaw is set but her eyes are steady—not challenging, but honest. She doesn't flinch from the mention of the bell-voice; instead, she leans into his fear with the ease of someone who's spent years listening to crew members confess their worst thoughts over a hot meal. One hand rests briefly on Tamsin's scroll case at her hip—a gesture that might be grounding herself, or showing she carries knowledge. She's reading him the way she reads every person who sits at her table: what's the real fear underneath, and what does he need to hear?)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I'm Aldous, Sergeant. Fortune-teller by trade. We were caught out on the flood when that sound started carrying from the temple—not natural, nothing natural at all. We moved for your gate as fast as we could. None of us took a scratch, and that thing never got close enough to try.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous meets the sergeant's gaze with steady composure, rain streaming down his face. He keeps his hands visible and his bearing calm—the ease of someone familiar with military order. There's no evasion in him, only steadiness.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Sergeant. We're travelers trying to make Hollowmoot before dark—you heard what's out there on the water same as we did. No injuries, none of us. I'm Mire, and these three are with me; we don't mean trouble in your town.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps up the gate-stair toward Coss, her blade already sheathed with the click of a practiced hand. She moves like someone who's answered to a Warden's watch-call before—shoulders settled, gaze steady, no defensiveness in it, just the clear bearing of someone who still remembers how to hold a line even if she's no longer wearing the badge. The rain's plastered her dark hair to her skull, and there's something both respectful and distant in how she answers: she knows the protocol, knows how to speak to the watch. But there's also something in her jaw that suggests she doesn't expect the courtesy to go both ways anymore.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Discipline learned from survival, Sergeant — the kind the rain teaches if you know how to listen. I was a soldier once, maybe, in a life before. I'm a fortune-teller now.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous refuses a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Coss's eyes narrow at Aldous's easy deflection — soldier once, maybe, in a life before — and something in the old drill-cadence of his answer snags in the sergeant's memory. "Discipline like that doesn't come from watching rain fall," Coss says flatly, rain sluicing off his helm. "You move like a man who took Verrick's orders." Aldous holds his ground and gives nothing more, spending a fate point to keep Verrick's name out of his mouth — but the storm itself betrays him: with the drowned hymn still carrying and every other sound in Hollowmoot swallowed by Endless Rain's downpour, Coss can't hear a lie in his voice one way or the other, and that uncertainty curdles into official caution. "Then you won't mind an escort while you find a bed," Coss says, and waves over a soaked junior Warden to shadow the party through the stilt-walks — polite, but never more than a few steps behind, eyes on Aldous especially. The gate-stair crowd thins fast around you as doors bar early up and down the walkway; whatever dry lodging is left in Hollowmoot tonight, you'll have to find it with company.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: That sound shook you as much as us, Warden—you're still rattled. Has it been calling like that long, or is this something new to Hollowmoot?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves with the group through the stilt-walks, her pace steady and unhurried. She makes no show of resisting the escort—instead, she simply falls into step beside the junior Warden with the natural ease of someone who's spent years listening to crew members confess their fears over a cook's fire. Her eyes take in the shuttered doors, the hurried townsfolk barring themselves in early, but her attention keeps returning to the Warden's face, reading the fear beneath the professional bearing. There's no challenge in her gaze, only the quiet, spacious attention of someone who knows how to make room for people to speak what frightens them. One hand rests on Tamsin's scroll case at her hip—grounding herself in her dead teacher's warnings about drowned places and Order ciphers.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: We need dry beds and a meal if Hollowmoot has them tonight. Sergeant Coss's fear runs deeper than just that bell—this town knows something about the temple it's not saying aloud.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous nods to the junior Warden with the ease of a man who's answered to authority before. He turns to his companions, shoulders settled, and gestures them toward the heart of Hollowmoot's stilt-walks—toward light, toward people, toward the smell of woodsmoke and food. He moves deliberately, not hurrying, the escort falling into step behind them like it's expected. As they navigate the wet boards, he lets his eyes read the town: which doors slam hardest, which lights stay lit longest, where the townspeople's gazes slide away from—and especially, where they *don't* look when the drowned hymn carries faintly through the rain.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Nothing yet.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen nods once at the junior Warden as the group moves into the stilt-walks, then settles into the rhythm of the others' stride. She says nothing, her dark eyes tracking the narrow walkway and the rain-heavy eaves around them, still listening for any echo of that drowned hymn beneath Hollowmoot's immediate sounds. She keeps a pace or two behind Mire, letting the others carry the introductions.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Shelter's ahead. We move together, keep sharp, don't give the Wardens a reason to ask questions.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire takes the lead through Hollowmoot's warren of stilt-walks, rain streaming off her hood, shoulders settled into the stance of someone who remembers watch-drills even without a badge. She reads the town as she passes—eyes sharp on smoke rising from chimneys, on signs still glowing in the downpour, on doors that haven't barred yet. Her hand rests easy on her sword's hilt, not hostile, just ready. The Warden escort stays a few steps back, but she doesn't slow for it. Find shelter, get dry, survive the night. That's the line she holds.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Coss doesn't answer Ysolde's question — he just looks past her at the belltower's shadow on the clouds and says nothing at all, which is answer enough. The junior Warden marches the four of you deeper into Hollowmoot as the last of the town bars itself in around you, shutters slamming, bolts thrown, the crier's bell falling silent house by house. Mire cuts the wandering short and turns them up a familiar ladder-stair to her own stilt-house — the last dry roof she still holds title to, however much the Cartel's ledger says otherwise — and gets the door open and the fire lit before full dark closes the town's throat. The Warden posts himself under the eave outside rather than come in, boots planted, watching the rain and, more than the rain, watching the drowned temple's black shape out past the flood. Inside, the four of you finally get out of the wet: dry boards underfoot, smoke curling up through the thatch, and the drowned hymn's next verse reaching you only as a faint, breath-thin thing through log walls — no closer to an answer about what it is, but for tonight, at least, on the wrong side of a barred door from it.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Sella's son wore the swarm-song two winters past. I kept him alive long enough for the fever to break, and kept the Wardens from burning the inn around him. She thinks she's owed sanctuary—or that I'll understand what she must do to survive.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You know what desperation costs. I hope what you're asking for is worth it.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts the compel on 'A Weary Innkeeper'.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Old Harrow was a fisher who pulled me from the shallows after the Reed-Kin cast me out—half-drowned, nothing but Tamsin's scroll case and exile marking my skin. He didn't ask why. He taught me to read the water the way his bloodline learned it, not the way the Clans guard their secrets. He's been dead three winters now, but I kept the key to his hut. The platform sits high enough to see the belltower clear across the flood, and Harrow spent his life watching that temple—he said it made a hunger in the water, drew things up from the deep places. I've studied his journals alongside Tamsin's warnings both. If that voice is calling from the belltower, that sightline is where we'll see what answers it.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Harrow's platform sits above the flood with a clear sight to the belltower—I've studied that temple from his hut, and I know what we're looking for. The structure's compromised after three winters of rain, but we move careful and we don't put all our weight in one place. If the boards start to go, we abandon for the roof. It's dangerous, but we need that vantage.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts the compel on 'A Fisher's Stilt Hut'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Sella, the weary innkeeper who keeps Hollowmoot's last dry common room and hears every rumor that crosses her threshold, pushes past the Warden at Mire's door and corners the party by the fire, wringing her hands raw. begs the party to go to a fisher's stilt hut standing alone out past the northern ford, its high platform giving a clear view across the marsh straight to the temple's belltower — the last place anyone saw her boy before the swarm-song took him., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sella won't be turned away from the fire — she kneels on Mire's own dry boards, rain still running off her shawl, and says the boy's name like a prayer: Tomas, who Morwen once pulled back from the fever two winters gone, who slipped out past the northern ford three nights ago chasing that same drowned hymn into the belltower's shadow. Ysolde already knows where this ends: Old Harrow's stilt hut, key still warm in her pocket, its high platform the only place in the Sallowmere with a clean line of sight straight to Saint Orrin's belltower. The Warden posted at the eave doesn't stop you passing back out into the dark — he just watches the temple's black shape and says nothing, same as Coss did. Beyond Hollowmoot's barred doors the causeway gives way to open water and reed, the ford black and restless where the Pikemaw is said to hunt, and somewhere out past it a platform three winters unrepaired waits with a dead man's memory of what the belltower hungers for.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Sella—Morwen knows what she did for your boy, and so do I. I have Harrow's key warm in my pocket right now. We'll go to that platform, we'll move careful, and we'll see what's calling from the belltower. If Tomas went toward that voice, that's exactly where we need to be to understand why it answered him.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde kneels beside Sella by the fire and pulls the iron key from her pocket—still warm from hours of being held close—and presses it gently into the woman's palm. Her other hand finds Tamsin's scroll case at her hip, anchoring herself in the dead scholar's warnings about drowned temples and Order ciphers. When she looks up to meet Sella's eyes, there's the steady recognition of someone who's spent years listening to crew members confess their deepest fears over a cook's fire. She glances to Aldous, Morwen, and Mire—no question there, only certainty—and turns back to Sella with a voice that carries no doubt: "Harrow's platform is three winters weathered but it'll hold if we respect the water. That hut sits high enough to see the belltower clear across the flood. If your son heard that hymn calling and followed it, we'll see what answered him from there. And we'll understand what we're walking into.")

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Your boy heard the hymn calling from the belltower, and I know what that hunger sounds like in deep water. I can't turn away from that—not now, not ever. We'll go to Harrow's platform and we'll look for Tomas. If there's any sign of him, any omen at all, the rain will show it to me.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves to where Sella kneels by the fire, his rain-soaked face grave. He crouches to meet her at eye level and takes her raw, trembling hands in his own. "Tell us everything from three nights ago—every detail about where he went, what he said, which way he turned. If we're walking into that flood and up to a platform three winters unrepaired, we need to know what drew him, so we know what we're looking for.")

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I kept him alive once. I'll go look for him.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen rises from where she was by the fire and steps closer to Sella. Her dark eyes hold the older woman's gaze for a moment — not unkindly, but with the weight of someone who has seen what the swarm-song does to the people it takes. She glances toward the window where the belltower's black shape waits in the rain, then back at Sella. There's no question in her posture, no hesitation. She reaches for her cloak.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The boy heard the belltower calling—we don't leave him to it. Ysolde, does Harrow's platform still give us sight line to that tower? I know every stone and shallow in the northern water. I'll get us across the ford safe.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire rises to her feet, the fire casting her shadow long across the room. She reaches down to help Sella to her feet with a steady, sure grip—a soldier's grip. Then she turns to face the group, jaw set, eyes sharp. She's already moving toward the door, ready to lead. "Gather what you need. We move now, while we've got maybe an hour before full dark gives that thing in the river its best hunting. The Warden outside won't stop us leaving—he's watching the belltower, not us.")

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sella clutches the key back into Ysolde's palm — "Bring him home, or bring me word" — and lets Mire pull her to her feet before backing toward the fire to wait out the night alone with her fear. The four of you move fast: cloaks resettled over damp shoulders, blades checked, Aldous murmuring the rhythm of the drowned hymn under his breath like a man counting a tide. Outside, the posted Warden doesn't so much as turn his head as you slip past him down the ladder-stair — his eyes are still fixed on the belltower's black shape, same as Coss's were, same as everyone's in this town who knows enough to be afraid and not enough to say why. Hollowmoot's doors are bolted tight behind you now, the crier's bell long silent, and the stilt-walks empty out into open water and reed as you strike north for the ford — Mire reading the shallows from old patrol-memory, Ysolde's hand never far from Tamsin's scroll case, Morwen watching the dark for any shape that moves wrong. Somewhere ahead, past the restless black channel where the Pikemaw is said to wait, Old Harrow's stilt hut leans out over the flood with its dead owner's sightline to Saint Orrin's belltower — and the hymn's next verse is already rising to meet you.

ambiguities.issue: Tension was lowered by 1 at event 16 ('resolved -1') with no THREAT/FACTION taken out, no player goal explicitly filled, and no clock advance logged anywhere in the scene. The only mechanical event was Aldous's successful Create Advantage roll (event 11) against an opposing HAZARD tag (H-01), which is neither a THREAT/FACTION resolution nor a clock event under the table. The spec does not define what counts as 'filled a player's goal' precisely enough to say whether a successful create-advantage against a GM hazard tag qualifies.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the GM's note 'resolved -1' as sufficient justification (informal reading of 'filled a player's goal' as Aldous achieving his read-the-omens objective) and left the -1 adjustment in place.

ambiguities.section: §3 Invokes / free invokes vs paid invokes
ambiguities.issue: Event 11's notes read 'aspect A-1.1.1 (1 free)' while fp_spent is 1 and fp_change is -1 (Aldous 3->2), i.e. the invoke was actually paid for, not free. It's unclear whether '(1 free)' is leftover numbering notation or an indication that a free invoke should have applied instead of a paid one.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Followed the fp ledger (fp_spent=1, balance drop) as authoritative over the ambiguous note text, treating the invoke as paid.

ambiguities.section: §7 Scene loop step 5 / Beat Frames (§5) and Backup modules (§7)
ambiguities.issue: Events 33 and 34 log 'Trigger fired: M-1' and 'Trigger fired: B-02' during scene-end cleanup, but no corresponding deployment (module cards revealed, Beat Frame draws/frame sentence) appears anywhere in the scene 2 log before scene end. The spec says a fired trigger must be 'deployed', but doesn't say whether deployment must happen within the same cleanup step or may be deferred to the opening of the next scene.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated 'Trigger fired' as marking the trigger as due; actual deployment (draws, frame sentence, module cards going face-up) is assumed to occur at the start of scene 3, off the excerpt shown here.

ambiguities.issue: The M-1 trigger note reads 'scene_start:3', an internal shorthand not matching the 'WHEN [event] THEN [deploy]' format the spec requires, and it is unclear whether the underlying condition ('3rd scene starts', or similar) can legitimately be evaluated as fired during scene 2's cleanup rather than at the actual start of scene 3.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Accepted the engine's internal trigger bookkeeping at face value as an observer-confirmable count-based event, absent visibility into the module's literal trigger text.

ambiguities.issue: The Beat Frame 'PLEA FOR HELP' (event 42) is drawn into and resolved with no logged trigger-fired event for it (unlike module M-1 at event 36, which cites 'trigger fired at previous cleanup: scene_start:3'). §7 requires every trigger to be checkable from the play log ('WHEN [event] THEN [deploy]'), but no such row explains why this Beat Frame fired here rather than at some other point.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as implicitly triggered by the same scene-start condition that deployed module M-1, since no other candidate trigger appears in the log; flagged rather than treated as a hard violation because the spec does not state that Beat Frame triggers and module triggers must be logged as distinct rows.

ambiguities.section: §6 Adjusting Tension table / §11 (no equivalent ruling for 'ignored')
ambiguities.issue: Module M-1 put a THREAT card (T-05, presumed by ID prefix) face-up on the rail this scene, and no roll was made against it during scene 3 (the scene was pure roleplay/compels). §6's table gives +1 tension if the party 'fled, bypassed or ignored a face-up THREAT or FACTION,' but the spec never defines what counts as 'ignored' (only §11 defines what counts as a roll 'against' a card for clock purposes, not for this tension trigger). The log shows tension held at 1 with 'no change' (event 55), implicitly treating T-05 as not ignored.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Since the party was engaged in a directly related plot beat (Sella's plea) rather than deliberately avoiding T-05, the table ruled this does not count as 'ignored' and applied 0 change, consistent with event 55.

ambiguities.issue: Two new story cards were added (SN-03 'Sella, Hollowmoot Innkeeper's Kin' and SN-04 'What happened to Tomas in the belltower?', events 59-60), but the log does not record which pile (a specific player's Story Pile vs. the GM Story Pile) each was filed into, even though §6A requires 'It goes to a player's pile if it ties to one character, otherwise to the GM Story Pile.'
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Assumed SN-03 (tied to Morwen's surfaced PX-03 card) went to Morwen's Player Story Pile, and SN-04 (an open world question not clearly tied to one PC) went to the GM Story Pile, per the letter of the rule, but this was not confirmed in the log.

cost_checks.note: This is a standard (non-deck-draw) compel on Aldous's own tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens'; draw_id is empty and the compel was refused, so no Session Deck draw and no §6A Story Pile draw were required or expected here. No cost-uses-drawn-card check applies.
Beat Frame fill for WHO used PX-03's power tag 'hears every rumor' to characterize Sella, matching the drawn ROOTS card.

Beat Frame fill for WHERE used PX-09's power tag 'view across the marsh' to describe the stilt hut, matching the drawn ROOTS card (via the type-mismatch fallback rule in §5 step 3, since ROOTS naturally fills WHO).
Surfacing compel on Morwen used PX-03's weakness tag 'Sells Out Lodgers' as the compel default, per §4.
Surfacing compel on Ysolde used PX-09's weakness tag 'Collapses Under Weight' as the compel default, per §4.

friction.text: The tension-adjustment justification ('resolved -1') doesn't map cleanly onto any row of the §6 tension table, making it hard to verify without a clearer definition of 'filled a player's goal.'
The '(1 free)' annotation on a fp-paid invoke (event 11) creates confusion between free-invoke bookkeeping and paid-invoke bookkeeping in the log format.

A GM Beat Frame/module trigger attempt was refused by the engine mid-scene ('not an unused fictional trigger'), suggesting the GM tried to fire a trigger outside the prescribed cleanup step 5 timing (§7 Scene loop) — the spec's trigger-deployment timing could be stated more explicitly to prevent such attempts.
Tension changes are being logged with a rationale label ('resolved -1') that doesn't match any visible in-scene event satisfying the §6 table, making it hard to audit Tension drift over a campaign.

Trigger-fired events (M-1, B-02) are recorded without their deployment payload in the same scene, obscuring whether the fixed cleanup order in §7 was actually followed or whether the trigger check leaked into the wrong scene boundary.

The engine had to refuse a GM-attempted trigger fire for being tied to loose fiction ('the party enters a settlement') rather than an approved, already-defined trigger — suggesting the GM agent is drifting from the required 'WHEN [event] THEN [deploy]', observer-confirmable trigger discipline in §7.
No logged trigger event for the 'PLEA FOR HELP' Beat Frame makes it impossible to verify from the log alone that the frame fired on a checkable condition as §7 requires.

The tension-adjustment rule for a bypassed/ignored face-up THREAT or FACTION has no clear standard for scenes (like this one) where the card is present but simply not the scene's focus, forcing a table-level judgment call each time.
Story card 'Add' events (SN-03, SN-04) don't record destination pile, making it hard to audit pile size limits (5 per player, 12 for GM) or ownership ties purely from the log.
